evals.prompt: Create a Power Pages site for our company called 'Contoso Solutions Portal'. It should be a public-facing company portal built with React. We want to showcase our services, share company news, and let customers reach out to us.
evals.expected_output: The skill discovers the site requirements (name: Contoso Solutions Portal, framework: React, purpose: Company Portal, audience: External, location: new folder in current directory), scaffolds the React template with placeholders replaced (__SITE_NAME__ = Contoso Solutions Portal, __SITE_SLUG__ = contoso-solutions-portal), runs npm install, initializes git, starts the dev server, and shares the URL. During component planning, the user selects Bold & Vibrant aesthetic with features like Services Catalog, News/Blog, Contact Form, and Team/About section, and a brand source; the skill writes an experience brief. The plan, with its Design direction section, is presented and approved. Implementation applies distinctive Google Fonts, the full color token set via CSS variables, motion/animations, and purposeful visuals, building Home and its hero first and reviewing the first impression from screenshots. Each page and component gets its own git commit. A screenshot-based design critique scores every page against the 10-category rubric. Accessibility is verified with axe-core on every route, all critical/serious violations are fixed and re-verified. The user reviews the site via the dev server URL and is asked about deployment.
expectations: Discovery phase asks for site name, framework, purpose, audience, and project location via AskUserQuestion
Site naming values are derived: __SITE_NAME__ = 'Contoso Solutions Portal', __SITE_SLUG__ = 'contoso-solutions-portal'
React template is copied from the assets/react/ directory and all __PLACEHOLDER__ tokens are replaced
gitignore file is renamed to .gitignore in the project root
npm install is run before git init so package-lock.json is included in the initial commit
Git repository is initialized with an initial scaffold commit
Dev server is started in background via 'npm run dev' and the localhost URL is shared with the user
Playwright browser_navigate and browser_snapshot are used to verify the scaffold loads (no screenshots taken)

Component planning asks for features (context-aware options for an external company portal), aesthetic direction (Bold & Vibrant selected), mood, and brand source (fresh identity, existing website, or brand colors or logo)

Design references are read from ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/design-aesthetics.md and ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/page-blueprints.md, and an experience brief (audience and job, primary and secondary action, principal doubt, proof strategy, design thesis, hero concept, signature moment) is written before tokens are chosen
A component plan table is presented showing pages, shared components, design elements, and routes

Color tokens cover every role in design-aesthetics.md section 3 (background, surfaces, text, muted text, borders, primary and on-primary, accent, focus, success, warning, danger), with each text and background pair checked against WCAG AA contrast
The implementation plan is rendered to docs/create-site-plan.html with render-createsite-plan.js, including its Design direction section, and user approval is requested
Design foundations are applied first: distinctive Google Fonts (not Inter/Roboto/Arial), CSS variables for colors, motion/animation utilities, and background treatments
The scaffold loading screen is completely replaced — no trace of Power Pages branded animation remains

Visuals follow design-aesthetics.md section 6: the site's own UI composed as a product moment or bespoke inline SVG first; any photography is task-specific Unsplash imagery found via WebSearch, sharing one art direction - never placeholder services
Each individual page gets its own dedicated git commit (not batched together)
Each shared component gets its own dedicated git commit
Playwright browser_snapshot checks each page's structure after creation; visual judgement comes from capture-design-review.js screenshots, not per-page browser_take_screenshot calls
Home and its hero are built first, then a first-impression review of / runs via capture-design-review.js at desktop (1440x900) and mobile (390x844) before the other pages

The Phase 5.7 design critique captures every route at desktop and mobile with one capture-design-review.js call per round, sending the URL and routes as a JSON request on stdin, scores the 10-category rubric, and fixes failing critical gates and categories below 3; after three rounds, a critical gate that still fails goes to the user through the critique-blocked prompt
axe-core audit script is run on every route, with the dev server URL and routes sent as a JSON request on stdin (--input -) rather than as command-line flags
All critical and serious accessibility violations are fixed and committed
axe-core is re-run after fixes to confirm zero critical/serious violations
An accessibility summary table is presented showing violations found vs fixed per page
User is asked to review the site at the dev server URL via AskUserQuestion
The Phase 7 review summary includes the design thesis and the critique scorecard, and lists every SAMPLE CONTENT marker with its file

Deployment is offered via AskUserQuestion with 'Deploy now' and 'Skip for now'; 'Deploy now' is recommended unless SAMPLE CONTENT placeholders remain, in which case they are listed first and 'Skip for now' is recommended
TaskCreate is used to create todos for all 8 phases before starting work

evals.prompt: Create a classic Power Pages summer camp site for college students. Use a supported template with the program registration capabilities we need, reuse its working program list, registration form and eligibility content snippet, and give the site a modern student-focused experience.
evals.expected_output: After the normal explicit model, environment and provisioning decisions, the new-site customization handoff treats the selected template as domain context and reusable components. It requires a custom Home and primary-journey layout, not a reskin. The approved plan separately identifies the retained native source/bindings and the new first-screen hierarchy, sections, component placements and responsive composition, mapped to native owner operations before final styling. Verification checks implemented composition against the plan and downloaded baseline without claiming rendered proof.
expectations: Template selection does not choose the site's visual identity, page outline or section sequence
The creation handoff includes creationIntent new-site, verified Bootstrap evidence, a custom-layout requirement and the existing newSiteDesign/designContext brief

The working program list, registration form and eligibility snippet are inventoried as reusable components with actual source, bindings, callers and locale scope, not copied together with the full starter page
Home and the primary visitor journey receive requirement-led first-screen hierarchy, section composition, actions, responsive behavior and explicit placements for reused components

Native operation inputs and preservation requirements resolve the actual composition work; a descriptive design brief plus only copy/image swaps, extra pages or CSS is not accepted as complete planning
Template-owned layout or shell source is assigned to the web-template/page-template owner when needed instead of leaving the old layout in place

Required native source and bindings remain intact at approved destinations; no invented type: form, type: list or type: reuse serialization, fabricated programs or static substitutes for working forms/lists are introduced
External-image pre-approval verification and exact-plan --imageChecks publication are retained; styling follows structural operations and keeps exact-diff/hash approval

The existing final verification compares Home and primary-journey source composition against the approved plan and baseline; the same template layout with new colors, text or images is reported as incomplete custom-layout work
There is no mandatory browser, dev server, extra approval gate or claim that source verification proves runtime appearance; deployment still needs separate consent

evals.prompt: Continue creating my new classic program-registration site from the baseline we just downloaded. Keep our approved logo and the registration form's fields and behavior, but make the site design and layout custom. Do not provision another site.
evals.expected_output: The unambiguous creation continuation routes to new-site customization even without a literal creationIntent argument. Logo and form behavior are scoped preservation requirements; the surrounding Home, journey and shell composition are custom. The plan reuses component source/bindings and resolves actual native layout operations without reprovisioning, changing form fields or freezing the whole page.
expectations: The request/session intent establishes new-site customization despite the missing literal creationIntent field; file timestamps or template metadata alone are not used to classify unrelated existing sites
No provisioning, model migration or duplicate website is attempted
The existing logo and registration form fields/behavior remain protected, but those exceptions do not preserve the surrounding starter layout
A custom Home and primary-journey composition is resolved in native owner operation inputs, with required component source and destinations
Existing metadata and rendering bindings are reused when compatible with the custom layout; table compatibility alone does not justify retaining the starter shell
Unknown relocation dependencies are reported to the caller/native owner rather than dropping the form, replacing it with static HTML or silently keeping the whole template layout
Final styling consumes the implemented custom composition; missing layout work is not declared complete merely because all CSS edits validate

evals.prompt: For the classic site we are creating, keep the Microsoft template unchanged. I only need the provisioned and downloaded baseline for now.
evals.expected_output: The explicit bare-baseline preference overrides the custom-layout default. The workflow completes the separately approved provisioning/download/validation steps and leaves the template unchanged, without starting customization or introducing a new-site styling plan.
expectations: The explicit Keep the template unchanged choice is honored without treating custom design as a prerequisite to returning the baseline
No native layout, component, branding, imagery or styling operations run after the baseline is established
The result is described as an unchanged baseline, not a completed custom design
The ordinary explicit model, environment and provisioning consent boundaries remain intact

evals.prompt: Continue creating our new classic camp site from the downloaded template. Give it a fresh design and layout. The starter carousel and newsletter sign-up form are not needed and can be removed. Keep the working program list, registration form, our logo and their required behavior. Do not delete any underlying records or deploy.
evals.expected_output: The customization plan accounts for removing the unused starter carousel and newsletter form placement, retaining required program/registration behavior and the logo, and composing a fresh native layout. It records removal rationale in existing operation summaries/inputs and preservation in preserve, then uses supported native replacement or scoped modification. Removed placements disappear from source rather than being hidden by CSS; backing records, permissions, data and unrelated callers remain untouched.
expectations: Template presence alone does not make a section or component mandatory; reuse is optional for unneeded components, not required for every native form/list/snippet
The plan inventories retain, relocate, replace and remove decisions against actual requirements and explicit preservation preferences, including the carousel and unused newsletter form placement
Removal scope and rationale are visible in the existing approved operation summaries and inputs without adding a schema, deletion action or approval gate

Supported native replace or scoped modify operations remove the planned source boundaries after inspecting dependent scripts, IDs, Liquid scope and callers; unknown dependencies are resolved before writing
The working program list, registration form, logo, native rendering contracts, locale scope and required behavior remain intact in the new composition
Removing the newsletter form placement does not delete its basic-form record, permissions, underlying data or other callers
Final source verification checks that approved removals are absent rather than hidden by CSS, while retained components and dependencies remain intact
Image verification, exact-plan approval and separate styling approval remain required; no deployment or runtime-proof claim is made
This new-site permission does not broaden unrelated existing-site narrow edits or override explicit preservation choices
